title: Accessibility review
learningObjectives: Complete accessibility review using the project's existing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and engineering practices.

understand.concept: An accessibility review checks semantic structure, accessible names, keyboard operation, visible focus, contrast, zoom and reflow, captions or alternatives, and relevant screen-reader behaviour. Automated tools complement manual testing.
understand.whyItMatters: Accessibility issues can block users from completing core tasks. Reviewing before publication is cheaper than repairing inaccessible patterns after release.
understand.analogy: An accessibility review checks whether every visitor has a usable route through the page.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; project requirements and release quality must be verified against the actual implementation and user needs.

explain.narrative: The checklist outlines core review areas. Each item needs actual inspection rather than a tick based only on code appearance.

examples.code: const review=['Landmarks and headings','Labels and names','Keyboard and focus','Contrast and non-colour cues','Zoom and reflow','Error feedback'];console.log(review);
examples.explanation: The checklist outlines core review areas. Each item needs actual inspection rather than a tick based only on code appearance.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates a project planning or implementation concept; learners must integrate and test it in their project.

practise.guidedTask: Complete a keyboard-only walkthrough and a contrast review. Record issues, severity, reproduction steps, and fixes.
practise.independentTask: Complete the task in a project repository. Keep the scope explicit, preserve user privacy, test the main workflow, and document evidence and known limitations.
hints: Plan before coding and keep changes focused.
Use semantic HTML and reusable responsive CSS.
Test keyboard access, edge cases, and deployment behaviour.

questions.prompt: Can a successful automated scan replace manual accessibility testing?
questions.explanation: Automated scans find only some accessibility problems; manual testing remains necessary.
